recipes.name: Mozzarella-Stuffed Pesto Turkey Meatballs
ingredients_raw: 1 pound fresh mozzarella, cut into small cubes

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Place the ground turkey, onion, garlic, egg, bread crumbs, Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, parsley, pesto, milk, salt, and black pepper in a bowl. Mix until evenly blended, then form into 1 3/4-inch meatballs. Make a hole in the meatball with your finger and place a cheese cube in the hole. Seal the meatball around the cheese and place on a nonstick baking sheet. Drizzle the olive oil over the meatballs.

Bake in the preheated oven until the meatballs are no longer pink in the center, about 30 minutes. Heat the marinara sauce in a saucepan over low heat. Bring to a simmer, and place the baked meatballs in the marinara sauce for about 2 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Mozzarella-Stuffed Pesto Turkey Meatballs
raw_recipe.description: Mozzarella cubes are tucked inside ground turkey meatballs seasoned with onion, garlic, pesto, and Italian cheese. The stuffed meatballs are baked in the oven and finished in a simmering pan of marinara sauce.

video.description: Elevating your meatballs to the next level is so simple you’ll never go back. First make your meatball base with ground turkey, onion, garlic, bread crumbs, pesto and Parmigiano-Reggiano. Roll into balls and stuff each with a cube of mozzarella. Bake and serve with warm marinara sauce. Good on pasta or makes an awesomely indulgent meatball sub!

review.reviewBody: Awesome recipe! My entire family begs me to make this! I have found that wrapping the meat around the mozzarella ball is easier than stuffing it in though. Definitely a fantastic family favorite

I made these meatballs for dinner and loved them. They had a very smooth texture and a great flavor! I never liked to make meatballs before because of the time involved but I thought these were very easy to do. I used pieces of string cheese for the mozzarella. I did not drizzle olive oil over the meatballs before baking because I was afraid the oil would splatter in the oven. About 15 minutes into the baking time, I rolled the meatballs over so that they would brown a little more evenly. I baked them on foil-lined baking sheets sprayed with cooking spray and there was no mess to clean up!

Overall the flavor was delicious!

I followed the ingredient list exactly except I didn’t have whole mozzarella so I used shredded. Like other reviewers I found it easiest to roll mixture into a rough ball shape, flatten it gently into a little disk, put some cheese in the middle, and then wrap the meat back around and firm into a nice ball shape. (Like making pupusas.) We got approximately 53 meatballs out of it.

We recently got an air fryer which my husband is *obsessed* with, so he put a first test batch in there to quickly feed our impatient children and they came out PERFECTLY - Juicy on the inside and just a hint of crisp on the outside.

The rest went on pans into the oven per the recipe. Unfortunately while they were cooking quite a bit of the cheese oozed out onto the pan. I saw other reviewers who used whole mozzarella say this also happened to them so I’m not sure if it was made worse because we used shredded or if it’s just the nature of mozzarella. (This ended up being fine for us because my five-year-old weirdly decided that he didn’t like the meatballs with cheese inside them but did like them with the same cheese outside of them.) Either way the flavor was absolutely delicious!

Next time - and there will be a next time - I may do any of the following: (1) Air fry only - no oven (2) use cut up cheese sticks as some other reviewers have suggested to avoid a lake of melted cheese in the baking pan (3) make a portion of them without cheese in the middle for my f

So yummy! Tons of flavor and very easy prep with pantry staple ingredients. I basically made the recipe as written with no substitutions. For ease of prep and cooking I mixed in shredded mozzarella (as desired) as opposed to stuffing each meatball. I also lined a 24 mini muffin pan with silicone liners for baking. The meatballs were about 1-1.25” and baked at 375 degrees for 20 minutes (my oven bakes a little hot). Clean up was a breeze!

I used lean ground beef and bulk Italian sausage (1 lb of each) instead of 3 lbs of turkey, I used all the rest of the ingredients that the recipe calls for and I got 20 even sized meatballs (using an ice cream scoop) and reheated them by simmering in a jar of Betolli's Five Cheese marinara sauce and they were the best I've ever had! I will make these again and again! My family loved them!

We liked this, but it was dry. Next time (yes, I will make it again!) I will pulverize some mushrooms to blend with the turkey mixture. Mushrooms release lots of moisture and flavor while keeping the turkey moist. For 1# ground turkey I use 4 oz fresh mushrooms.

I made this last night, and couldn't believe how tasty it was. I passed the recipe on to my daughter and she plans on making it this weekend. I had to cut the recipe in half since it's only my husband and me, but I think next time, I'll make the full recipe and freeze the remainder. I baked most of them in the oven, but put 4 in the air fryer. The airfryer meatballs were awesome! Just a slight crisp on the outside and nicely done on the inside. The ones that came out of the oven were bland looking, so put them in the airfryer for 5 minutes. They browned very nicely with that slight crisp to them. I will be using the airfryer for all my meatballs in the future.

I made the recipe with 1/2 ground chicken and 1/2 Italian turkey sausage since that was what I had on hand. Other ingredients were the same as written. This was delicious! The only thing I would do differently is to spray the baking pan so they don't stick. For those who couldn't form the meatballs, I wonder if it would help to just add another tablespoon of breadcrumbs?

These ingredients all combined together came out delicious. In the interest of time I added grated mozzarella to the mixture rather than adding cubes at the end. It still came out moist and tasty. The only thing I would change is I would saute the onions before combining them into the mixture. Mine came out a little crunchy, which is not pleasing to my kids palates.

Meatballs came out great. I didn’t have pesto so i subbed it with Worcester sauce and a tsp of ginger. Rather than stuff it with a cheese cube i mixed in the same amount of grated cheese at the end. Using a tablespoon to portion out each meatball made the sizes consistent. The kids loved it. Will definitely make it again!
This is a fantastic recipe. Best homemade meatballs ever. My family loved them
Turned out really good! The whole family loved it! I used 1 lb of ground turkey instead of 3 and just made smaller meatballs and it still turned out great!
I made some meatballs without the cheese for one of my sons who is allergic to dairy foods. The rest I made as directed in the recipe. Everyone really enjoyed it. Great flavor! A keeper.

THE BEST recipe I have come across so far!! Had to tweak some condiments around because I didn’t have them, like pesto & marinara sauce. But the meatball itself is also great as a stand alone! I used 1lb. of ground turkey & used similar measurements for just 1lb. & it turned out amazing! Had some cheese leftover so I placed it on top lol.

I made yesterday for a tailgate and everyone loved them. It made 50 (2 bite size) meatballs. As others suggested, I added extra pesto and Parmesan cheese. I did not add the mozzarella in the center, because others complained of oozing and I didn't want that in the crockpot. I will try it next time. I cooked the meatballs on plain parchment for 20 minutes, with no olive oil and they cooked perfectly and didn't get dark on the bottom. I served these in a crock pot with Trader Joes basil marinara and little rolls for those that wanted a sandwich. They were perfect.

Definitely a keeper! I only had 2 pounds of ground turkey but I used basically the same amount of the other ingredients and it was delicious. I didn’t have pesto and it was fine without it. Also, I went a little heavy on the olive oil drizzle so I would go lighter next time.
